subject: politics
prompt: When the chapter speaks of **gender division**, what does it mean?

image.alt: A home where different people cook, wash, look after a child and read while another person leaves for work

options.text: The unequal roles that society assigns to men and women
The biological difference between men and women
The unequal child sex ratio in the country
The absence of voting rights for women in democracies

hint: The chapter says it is not based on biology.
explanation: Gender division is a **hierarchical social division** based on **social expectations and stereotypes**, not on biology, so the first option is right. Biological difference is a different thing; the child sex ratio is only one **result** of unequal treatment; and in most democracies women now have voting rights.

subject: politics
prompt: Which description fits the **sexual division of labour** as defined in the chapter?

image.alt: Two zones: work inside the home and work outside the home

options.text: Men and women share all household tasks equally
The law forbids women from taking up work outside the home
Work inside the home is done by the women of the family or organised by them through domestic helpers, while men mostly work outside
Each person is assigned household tasks by the government

hint: Think about who is expected to run the home.
explanation: The glossary defines it as a system in which **all work inside the home is either done by the women of the family or organised by them** through domestic helpers. Equal sharing is the opposite, nothing in the law bars women from outside work (the problem is expectation and lack of recognition), and the government does not assign household tasks.

4 h 30 min (household work only)
1 h 15 min (sleep time only)

explanation: Men: 6:00 + 0:30 = 6 h 30 min. Women: 2:40 + 5:00 = 7 h 40 min. The difference is **1 h 10 min**, which the chapter rounds to "one hour more". Comparing only income work gives 3 h 20 min (and in the wrong direction), only household work gives 4 h 30 min, and the sleep gap of 1 h 15 min is not work at all.

subject: politics
prompt: Which provision was made by the **Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (Women's Reservation Act, 2023)**?

image.alt: Three law-making halls each with a third of seats highlighted

options.text: Equal wages for equal work for women and men
One-third of seats in panchayats and municipalities only
33 per cent of seats for women in the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies and Delhi Assembly
Half of all cabinet posts for women

hint: It is about seats in law-making bodies.
explanation: The 2023 Act provides **33 per cent reservation** of seats for women in the **Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies and the Delhi Assembly**. Equal wages come from the Equal Remuneration Act, 1976; reservation in local bodies already existed under the Panchayati Raj; and cabinet posts are not covered.

subject: politics
prompt: Select **all** the ways in which, according to the chapter, women are disadvantaged in India.

image.alt: A balance with two workers doing the same task on one side and a smaller pile of coins on the other

options.text: Literacy among women is lower than among men
Women are often paid less than men for the same work, despite the Equal Remuneration Act, 1976
The child sex ratio has fallen because many families prefer sons
Women are not allowed to vote in elections today
An average woman works fewer hours a day than an average man
Women never do paid work outside the home

hint: Check each option against the chapter's list of ways women face discrimination.
explanation: The chapter lists lower literacy (54 against 76 per cent), unequal pay for equal work even though the Equal Remuneration Act of 1976 says wages must be equal, and a falling child sex ratio. Women do vote; on average a woman works about an hour **more** than a man; and many women do paid work as well as domestic work.

people of different religions can easily live together as equal citizens
state power must never be used to dominate one religious group
there are many voices inside every community

subject: politics

subject: politics
prompt: What makes the caste system different from the division of labour found in other societies?

image.alt: A tool passed down generations, two people inside a ring, and two groups at separate tables

options.text: Everybody chose an occupation freely
Hereditary occupational division was sanctioned by rituals
It is found in every society in the same form
Members freely married and ate with every other group

hint: Other societies also pass on occupations; what did caste add?
explanation: In most societies occupations pass from one generation to the next. Caste is an extreme form where **hereditary occupational division was sanctioned by rituals**, with marriage within the group and no eating together with other castes. Unlike gender and religion, caste division is special to India.

subject: politics
prompt: Why is there a disproportionately large presence of "upper caste" people among the urban middle classes?

image.alt: Two rows of steps over generations, one reaching a cap and the other meeting a gate

options.text: The Constitution reserves urban jobs for them

They are the largest group in the population
Caste hierarchy has disappeared completely, so all groups start equal

hint: Think of effects of centuries of advantage and disadvantage.
explanation: The chapter says groups that had **access to education** under the old system did well in modern education too, while those who were **prohibited** from it lagged behind. The Constitution outlaws caste discrimination, upper castes are not the majority, and caste has changed but has **not disappeared**.

prompt: Why are the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes called "Scheduled"?
